sentences.text: Nullotitan was a lithostrotian titanosaur belonging to the class Saurischia, a group of large, long-necked dinosaurs.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a cervical vertebra, tail vertebrae, ribs, a scapula, and leg bones.
This individual measured more than 20 meters in length and weighed approximately 20 tons, placing it in the medium body size category for sauropods, which ranges from 12 to 22 meters long.
One neck vertebra in the holotype is 45 centimeters long and 22 centimeters high, excluding the broken arch, and contains many small internal air chambers called camellae.
The front and middle tail vertebrae feature large depressions on their sides and undersides that do not penetrate the bone wall.
The fibula exhibits a distinct S-shaped curve when viewed from the front or back, creating a notable wavy appearance.
The first tail vertebra measures approximately 25 centimeters in length and 40 centimeters in width, while a referred humerus is 114 centimeters long with a robustness index of 0.28.
Excavations revealed a new fauna across 2,000 square kilometers containing six bone concentrations linked to the original discovery.
Titanosaur eggshells and sauropod teeth have been found in the same geological formation, suggesting a diverse ecosystem.
Remains of Nullotitan were found in the Chorrillo Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, where geologist Francisco E. Nullo first noticed sauropod bones at the Estancia Alta Vista site in 1980.
José Bonaparte excavated a large cervical vertebra in 1981 and initially reported it as cf. Antarctosaurus before further study.

The species Nullotitan glaciaris was formally named and described by Fernando Emilio Novas and colleagues in 2019; the genus name honors paleontologist Francisco Nullo and links it to a Greek titan, while the species name refers to the Perito Moreno Glacier visible near the fossil discovery site.

Researchers suggest that epaxial tendons may have been anchored to the tail, holding it upward, while the large retractor muscle Musculus caudofemoralis, which pushed the femur backward, extended to the sixteenth vertebra.

Novas and colleagues initially classified Nullotitan as a colossosaurian titanosaur in 2019 without a phylogenetic test, though later analyses recovered it as a lithostrotian titanosaur outside the group Colossosauria.
The holotype fossils date to the Campanian–Maastrichtian stages of the lower Chorrillo Formation, meaning Nullotitan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Nullotitan lived alongside the ornithopod dinosaur Isasicursor, and the same formation contains fossils of the theropod Maip and the birds Kookne and Yatenavis.
It is currently unknown whether the newly discovered series of five middle tail vertebrae at a different location have been excavated.
